platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
details: **AI Security Findings & posture dashboard — GA (June 24, 2026)** — a new Security tab in the Agent Platform console surfaces AI security posture management: a "Top security findings" widget, AI risks by severity (vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, **toxic combinations**, an attack-exposure score), real-time AI threats against control planes/runtimes, an **"Agents with excessive permissions"** least-privilege widget that lists specific agent identities and their unused permissions, and a Compliance widget. Security Command Center AI-risk findings are surfaced directly in the tab. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/view-security-findings

**Model Armor on Agent Gateway — GA (June 24, 2026)** — Model Armor can now be enabled on an Agent Gateway resource to apply content-security guardrails to all prompts and responses passing through the gateway (block/redact or inspect+log), mitigating prompt injection, jailbreaks, harmful content, and sensitive-data leakage at the agent-to-tool communication layer. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/configure-model-armor

**Agent Observability + default OpenTelemetry tracing — GA (June 18, 2026)** — a new observability surface giving visibility into the performance, behavior, and health of deployed agents **and MCP servers**, collecting traces, logs, and metrics (via OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions) from Agent Platform, Agent Gateway, and Model Armor. OpenTelemetry tracing is now **enabled by default** for newly deployed ADK agents on Agent Engine. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/optimize/observability/overview

**Agent Registry — GA (June 18, 2026)** — a central governance/inventory hub: a queryable catalog that stores, discovers, and manages **AI agents, MCP servers, and tools** across the org (own, Google, and third-party), capturing metadata such as versions, frameworks (e.g. ADK), and MCP tool names/annotations, with allow/deny egress policies enforced via Agent Gateway. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/agent-registry

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — Agent Registry (GA)
findings.description: Google shipped a native central inventory/governance catalog of AI agents, MCP servers, and tools (own, Google, and third-party) with per-entity metadata (versions, frameworks, MCP tool names/annotations) and Agent-Gateway-enforced allow/deny egress policies. This is a first-class new inventory-entity surface on a platform Zenity monitors: registered-agent objects, registered MCP-server objects, registered tool objects, and their egress policy bindings. AISPM must discover and map these registry entities and reconcile them against actual deployed/running agents (registry-vs-reality drift, unregistered shadow agents, and over-broad egress allow-lists are the toxic-combination surfaces)

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — AI Security Findings & posture dashboard (GA)
findings.description: A native AISPM surface now GA in the console — security findings, AI risks by severity (vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, toxic combinations, attack-exposure score), real-time AI threats, an "Agents with excessive permissions" least-privilege widget naming specific agent identities and their unused permissions, and a Compliance widget, fed by Security Command Center. This introduces new inventory/finding entity types (security findings, excessive-permission agent identities, compliance status) that AISPM should ingest and correlate; it is also a direct native analogue of Zenity's own posture/least-privilege detection on a monitored platform, worth mapping for coverage parity and to avoid blind reliance on the platform's own scoring

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — Model Armor on Agent Gateway (GA)
findings.description: Content-security guardrails (prompt-injection, jailbreak, harmful-content, and sensitive-data-leakage detection, with block/redact or inspect+log actions) can now be enabled on the previously-reported Agent Gateway, inspecting every prompt and response that transits the gateway. This is a new runtime enforcement/detection chokepoint at the agent-to-tool data-flow layer. AIDR should treat Model-Armor-on-gateway as a new detectable data-flow control point — track which gateways have it enabled, what its templates block vs. only log, and the prompts/responses it inspects — since gaps or "inspect-only" templates define where injected/exfiltrating traffic can still pass

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — Agent Observability + default OpenTelemetry tracing (GA)
findings.description: A new observability surface exposing traces, logs, and metrics for deployed agents and MCP servers (OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions), with tracing now on by default for newly deployed ADK agents on Agent Engine, aggregating telemetry from Agent Platform, Agent Gateway, and Model Armor. This is a new activity/telemetry surface AIDR can consume as a detection source — per-agent sessions, tool executions, retrieval steps, token usage, latency, and error rates — for monitoring agent behavior and spotting anomalous tool-call/data-access patterns

platforms.name: Salesforce AgentForce
details: **Agentforce Commerce — GA (July 6, 2026)** — the Shopper Agent (B2C storefront, discovery→checkout→service), Buyer Agent (autonomous B2B purchasing/reordering with pre-negotiated pricing over WhatsApp and SMS, no portal login), and Merchant Agent (back-office catalog/promotions in natural language) went generally available. Each is wired natively into catalog, inventory, and orders — and, critically, exposed into **external agentic surfaces**: ChatGPT (catalog sync from Business Manager), Google Search including AI Mode, and the Gemini app. Source: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=cc.b2c_agent_guided_shopping.htm&type=5

**Agentforce Help Agent + Customer Service Portal — GA (July '26)** — a prepackaged autonomous service agent that resolves customer issues end-to-end across voice, web, portal, and messaging from a single setup screen, grounded automatically on Salesforce Knowledge, with a library of actions that run real workflows (manage cases, schedule appointments, update orders). Pay-per-resolution pricing. The Customer Service Portal is redesigned around a single conversation bar with dynamic real-time cards. Source: https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.service_agent_overview.htm&type=5

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce Commerce — Shopper/Buyer/Merchant agents (GA)
findings.description: Three new production commerce agent types went GA July 6, 2026, each natively wired into catalog, inventory, and orders. Introduces new inventory entities Zenity must discover and map: Shopper agents, Buyer agents, and Merchant agents, plus their catalog/inventory/order data connections and the actions each can take (place/reorder purchases, edit catalogs, run promotions). Toxic-combination surface — an autonomous Buyer Agent that can transact (checkout, reorder at pre-negotiated pricing) is a high-value overprivileged-agent target, and the Merchant Agent's plain-language catalog control is a business-logic manipulation path. AISPM should inventory these agents, their permissions, and their order/catalog reach

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce Commerce — external agentic surfaces (ChatGPT / Google / Gemini + WhatsApp/SMS)
findings.description: Agentforce commerce agents and product catalogs now integrate natively into third-party agentic surfaces — ChatGPT (via catalog sync and agentic MCP shopper tools), Google Search/AI Mode, and the Gemini app — and the Buyer Agent transacts autonomously over WhatsApp and SMS with no portal login. This creates new cross-platform agent-to-external-LLM data flows and autonomous purchase/checkout actions that cross the Salesforce org boundary. AIDR should monitor these as new external data-egress and indirect-prompt-injection channels (untrusted shopper input arriving from ChatGPT/Gemini/messaging), and track catalog/inventory data leaving the org to external LLM providers

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce Help Agent + Customer Service Portal (GA)
findings.description: A new prepackaged autonomous service agent, deployable from one screen across voice/web/portal/messaging, grounded on Salesforce Knowledge, with an action library that manages cases, schedules appointments, and updates orders. Introduces a new autonomous-service-agent entity Zenity must inventory — its enabled actions, Knowledge grounding sources, and cross-channel reach define its real capability and data-access surface, and out-of-the-box "deployable in minutes" provisioning means such agents can appear in a tenant without deliberate per-agent review (shadow-agent / overprivilege risk)

platforms.name: Salesforce AgentForce
details: **Multi-Agent Orchestration — GA (June 15, 2026)** — a primary Agentforce agent now coordinates a team of specialized subagents, holding shared context and dynamically routing each request to the best-fit specialist based on subagent descriptions/instructions/actions (no fixed decision trees). Powered by the new **Atlas Reasoning Engine 3.0**. Source: https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/multi-agent-orchestration/

**Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol support** — open-protocol support letting a primary Agentforce agent securely delegate work to third-party agents on other platforms (Google Vertex, Microsoft Azure Agent Mesh, third-party frameworks) via a client/server model with capability-discovery "Agent Cards." Shipped alongside Multi-Agent Orchestration GA. Source: https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/ai-agents/agent2agent-protocol/

**Agent Script — GA (waves from June 13, 2026)** — a scripting language for the new Agentforce Builder that blends natural-language instructions with deterministic programmatic expressions/business rules; authorable in a "Script view" with syntax highlighting, autocompletion, and validation. Source: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-script.html

**IT Service Domain Pack (50+ prebuilt agents)** — an out-of-the-box pack of 50+ specialized AI agents deployed in Slack, Teams, and the IT Service Desk to detect intent and resolve employee IT needs. Source: https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/summer-2026-product-release-announcement/

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
details: **Rebrand to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform + first-class Agents API** — Vertex AI now presents under the "Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform" framing and exposes a first-class **Agents API** (`projects.locations.agents`, v1beta1: create/list/get/patch/delete) plus a visual **Agent Studio** builder — agent resources distinct from generic model endpoints. Reasoning Engines were also extended with `streamQuery`/`asyncQuery`, stateful **Sessions**, and runtime revisions. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/rest

**Semantic Governance Policy (SGP) engine + Agent Gateway** — a new managed governance layer provisioned in the customer VPC that semantically evaluates each proposed agent tool call/skill invocation against the prompt, conversation history, and Natural Language Constraints (NLCs) before execution, and an **Agent Gateway** for governing agentic workloads. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/policies/semantic-governance-overview

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI)
details: **Codex Sites plugin — preview (June 2, 2026)** — a new plugin that lets Codex create, save, deploy, and inspect websites, web apps, dashboards, internal tools, and games hosted by OpenAI. Output runs as Cloudflare-Worker-compatible ES modules on OpenAI-operated hosting; every deployment URL is a production deployment. Available for ChatGPT Business/Enterprise (Enterprise gated behind admin RBAC). Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/sites

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce — Multi-Agent Orchestration (GA)
findings.description: A primary "orchestrator" agent now coordinates a team of specialized subagents with shared context and dynamic, description-driven routing (Atlas Reasoning Engine 3.0). Introduces new inventory entities Zenity must discover and map: orchestrator agents, their member subagents, the routing relationships between them, and the shared-context flows. Prime toxic-combination surface — an orchestrator that can route to an overprivileged subagent, or a subagent whose description lets it be recruited for out-of-scope tasks, is a direct privilege-escalation/data-exposure path

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce — Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol
findings.description: Agentforce agents can now securely delegate work to third-party agents on other platforms (Vertex, Azure Agent Mesh, external frameworks) via A2A, using capability-discovery "Agent Cards." A new cross-platform agent-interaction surface: AISPM must inventory which Agentforce agents expose or consume A2A, enumerate the remote/external agents they connect to, and treat each A2A edge as a trust boundary and data-egress path. AIDR should monitor A2A task/message flows as a new external-agent data-flow and indirect-prompt-injection channel (untrusted content arriving from a remote agent)

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce — Agent Script (GA)
findings.description: A new scripting language for the Agentforce Builder that mixes natural-language instructions with deterministic programmatic expressions to define agent behavior. A new agent-logic authoring surface AIRT should probe for prompt-injection into the natural-language segments, logic/guardrail bypass via crafted inputs, and unsafe action sequences expressible in script; AISPM should treat agent scripts as a governed configuration artifact whose actions/connections define the agent's real capability set

findings.title: Salesforce Agentforce — IT Service Domain Pack (50+ prebuilt agents)
findings.description: An out-of-the-box pack of 50+ specialized AI agents deployed into Slack, Teams, and the IT Service Desk. Introduces a large new prebuilt-agent inventory Zenity must enumerate and govern — each prebuilt agent carries its own actions, connections, and Slack/Teams reach, and out-of-the-box deployment means agents can appear in a tenant without deliberate per-agent review (shadow-agent and overprivilege risk)

findings.title: Google Vertex AI — Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Agents API + Agent Studio)
findings.description: Vertex AI's rebrand to the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform introduces a first-class Agents API (`projects.locations.agents`) and visual Agent Studio builder, plus stateful Reasoning-Engine Sessions and runtime revisions — agent resources distinct from the generic model endpoints Zenity previously mapped. AISPM must discover and inventory these new first-class agent entities, their Sessions, and runtime revisions as a distinct resource class on the Google surface

findings.title: Google Vertex AI — Semantic Governance Policy (SGP) engine + Agent Gateway
findings.description: A new managed governance layer (provisioned in the customer VPC) that semantically evaluates each proposed agent tool call/skill invocation against the prompt, history, and Natural Language Constraints before execution, fronted by an Agent Gateway. This is both a control AISPM should map (which agents have SGP policies and Agent Gateway enforcement — gaps mean ungoverned agents) and a bypass target AIRT must probe: NLC evasion, context-poisoning to slip a malicious tool call past semantic analysis, and confirming that agent traffic is actually routed through the gateway rather than around it

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — Sites plugin (preview)
findings.description: A new Codex plugin (preview, June 2 2026) that lets the agent create, deploy, and host production websites, web apps, dashboards, internal tools, and games on OpenAI-operated infrastructure (Cloudflare-Worker-compatible ES modules; every deployment URL is live production). A new agent-driven code-deployment surface Zenity's endpoint coverage should track: the agent can push executable code to public production hosting from a single prompt, creating new hosted-app entities and a data-exfiltration/malicious-deploy path. AISPM should inventory which workspaces/members have the Sites plugin enabled (Enterprise gates it behind admin RBAC) and the sites they deploy

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **Managed Knowledge Base — GA** — a fully managed retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) knowledge base that agents query through the Gateway as a pre-built target type. Six native connectors (Amazon S3, SharePoint, Confluence, Google Drive, OneDrive, Web Crawler) ingest data with automatic syncing and managed vector storage; supports hybrid search, document ranking, advanced retrieval orchestration, and text/video/audio/image content; auto-generates role-based permissions with observability/eval metrics. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/knowledge-base.html

**Web Search Tool — GA** (announced AWS Summit New York, June 17, 2026) — a fully managed tool that grounds agent responses in current web knowledge with zero data egress from the customer's AWS environment, built on Amazon's web index + knowledge-graph data. Exposed as a built-in connector target on the AgentCore Gateway via MCP; returns ranked results with snippets, source URLs, titles, and publication dates. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/web-search.html

**AgentCore Policy — Bedrock Guardrails support** — Policy now supports Bedrock Guardrails, evaluating outputs of authorized agent actions and inputs to gateway targets for prompt-injection attempts, harmful content, and sensitive-data exposure. Checks run at the gateway layer, outside agent code, so every tool/context source routed through the gateway is automatically governed. Policies authored via natural language or policy-as-code. Distinct from the previously reported Cedar-based Policy. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-guardrails.html

**Gateway — new target types** — three new/GA gateway target classes: **HTTP passthrough targets** (route to any HTTP endpoint without protocol translation — front agent URLs, external APIs, A2A agents, external MCP servers, custom inference endpoints, with unified auth/policy/observability and optional session stickiness); **Inference targets** (front model providers with model discovery, model-ID translation, path rewriting, and per-model token limits); and **AgentCore Runtime-agent targets — GA** (send gateway traffic directly to a runtime agent, with API-schema-driven guardrails and request/response interceptor Lambdas). Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-http-passthrough.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-inference-connector.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-target-http-runtime.html

**Runtime — Interactive Shells (Terminals)** — AgentCore Runtime now supports interactive shell sessions giving agents persistent terminal access to their sandboxed environment; env vars, working directories, and running processes persist across commands for the session lifetime, with up to 10 concurrent shell sessions per runtime session. Distinct from one-shot command execution (`InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`). Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-get-started-command-shell.html

findings.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — Managed Knowledge Base (GA)
findings.description: New fully managed RAG knowledge base queryable by agents through the Gateway as a pre-built target type, with six native ingestion connectors (Amazon S3, SharePoint, Confluence, Google Drive, OneDrive, Web Crawler), automatic syncing, managed vector storage, hybrid/multimodal retrieval, and auto-generated role-based permissions. Introduces inventory entities Zenity does not yet monitor: managed knowledge bases, their six data-source connectors (each a distinct enterprise-data flow into agents), KB-as-gateway-target bindings, and the generated IAM permissions. Prime toxic-combination surface — an overbroad connector (e.g. a whole SharePoint/Drive) wired to a broadly-reachable agent is a direct data-exposure path AISPM must discover and map

findings.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — Web Search Tool (GA)
findings.description: New fully managed built-in tool (AWS Summit NY, June 17, 2026) that grounds agents in live web content, exposed as a built-in MCP connector target on the AgentCore Gateway. A new tool/connector entity that gives agents outward web reach — AISPM must inventory which gateways/agents expose the Web Search target and treat it as a sensitive external-reach capability. It is also an inbound untrusted-content channel: AIDR should monitor returned snippets/source URLs as an indirect-prompt-injection and data-provenance surface

findings.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — Policy + Bedrock Guardrails
findings.description: AgentCore Policy now integrates Bedrock Guardrails to evaluate agent-action outputs and gateway-target inputs for prompt injection, harmful content, and sensitive-data exposure, enforced at the gateway layer outside the agent's code (distinct from the previously reported Cedar-based Policy). This is both a governance control AISPM should map (which gateways/targets are guarded, and gaps where they are not) and a bypass target AIRT must probe — guardrail evasion at the gateway boundary, and confirming every new tool/context source is actually routed through the guarded gateway

findings.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — new Gateway target types (HTTP passthrough, Inference, Runtime-agent)
findings.description: Three new gateway target/connector classes greatly expand an agent's reachable surface through a single gateway: HTTP passthrough targets front arbitrary APIs, external MCP servers, A2A agents, and custom inference endpoints; Inference targets front model providers with per-model token limits and model-ID translation; Runtime-agent targets (GA) route directly to runtime agents. Each is a new connector entity Zenity must enumerate and govern — external-MCP-server and A2A-agent passthroughs in particular are notable toxic-combination sources (an agent reaching an unvetted external MCP server or peer agent through the gateway)

findings.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — Runtime Interactive Shells (Terminals)
findings.description: AgentCore Runtime now grants agents persistent interactive shell sessions — environment variables, working directories, and running processes persist across commands for the session lifetime, with up to 10 concurrent shells per runtime session. A new stateful command-execution surface distinct from one-shot `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand`, broadening tool-execution and post-exploitation risk (persistent process/state, lateral movement within the sandbox). AIRT should add coverage for agent shell-session abuse and command-injection-to-shell paths; AISPM should treat interactive-shell access as a sensitive capability binding on an agent runtime

platforms.name: Azure AI Foundry
details: **Foundry MCP Server** — a Model Context Protocol server for Foundry (no infra to deploy) that enforces Entra ID auth/authorization via On-Behalf-Of flow and exposes a growing set of read/write tools over Foundry models, deployments, evaluations, and agents to MCP clients and coding agents. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/mcp/get-started

**Foundry Skill in coding agents** — a reusable skill that plugs into coding agents to standardize Foundry workflows (deployment, evaluation, prompt optimization, dataset curation from traces, troubleshooting); bundled with the Azure Skills Plugin alongside the Foundry MCP Server. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/develop/use-microsoft-foundry-skill

**Hosted agents (Foundry Agent Service) + prompt-agent quickstart** — containerized, own-code agents deployed to Microsoft-managed infra; each deployment is assigned a dedicated Microsoft Entra ID (agent identity) and dedicated endpoint, and published agents can be shared through M365 Copilot / Teams and the Entra Agent Registry. New agent deployment/sharing surface distinct from prompt-based agents. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents

**Foundry Control Plane** — a unified control plane to track/manage agents from supported platforms across projects in one view, with cross-project visibility, unified compliance enforcement, integrated security signals, and per-project TPM rate-limit / token-quota enforcement for model deployments. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/control-plane/overview

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI)
details: **Codex Remote — General Availability** — phone→host agent control is now GA for all plans, secured by authenticated one-to-one QR pairing between each iOS/Android device and each connected Mac/Windows host. From a paired phone, users start threads in host projects, send follow-ups, answer agent questions, approve/deny commands, and review diffs/tests/terminal/screenshots. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/remote-connections

**Codex DigitalOcean provisioning plugin (public preview)** — connects a DigitalOcean account via OAuth and lets Codex provision and configure a Droplet (from the Codex Universal image, with CLI/tooling/SSH pre-wired) as an on-demand remote workspace, no doctl/API tokens required. Source: https://www.digitalocean.com/blog/run-codex-in-the-cloud

**Codex CLI 0.142.2** — MCP tools now use tool search by default where supported (new default MCP tool-discovery behavior), and remote stdio MCP servers accept absolute working directories in platform-native path formats; adds a PowerShell approval gate for unlowered-AST command regions. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

platforms.name: Windsurf (Devin Desktop)
details: **Devin Local autonomous mode (v3.4.22)** — Devin Local (the Rust-rewritten successor to Cascade, available on every tier including Free) gains an autonomous mode that runs the agent without step-by-step supervision and surfaces reviewable diffs before push, with subagent support for subtasks. New local unsupervised agent-execution surface. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/changelog

**`/mcp` command + live MCP server status dashboard (v3.4.22)** — a new in-session `/mcp` slash command with a live status dashboard for connected MCP servers, giving users a control/inspection surface over the agent's MCP tool connections. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-mcp

findings.title: Azure AI Foundry — Foundry MCP Server
findings.description: New Entra-authenticated MCP endpoint (no infra to deploy) that exposes read/write tools over Foundry models, deployments, evaluations, and agents to any MCP client or coding agent, operating within the authenticated user's permissions (On-Behalf-Of). A new tool-exposure/connector channel through which external agents reach Foundry resources — AISPM must inventory the MCP server, the tools it exposes, and which identities/agents can invoke it (a prime overprivileged-agent / data-reach toxic combination)

findings.title: Azure AI Foundry — Foundry Skill for coding agents
findings.description: New reusable skill entity that plugs into coding agents to drive Foundry workflows (deploy, evaluate, prompt-optimize, curate datasets from traces), bundled with the Azure Skills Plugin alongside the Foundry MCP Server. Introduces a shareable capability + supply-chain surface (an overbroad/malicious shared skill propagates Foundry access across coding agents); AISPM should inventory skills and their agent bindings

findings.title: Azure AI Foundry — hosted agents (Foundry Agent Service)
findings.description: New agent type — containerized, customer-code agents deployed to Microsoft-managed infra, each assigned a dedicated Microsoft Entra ID (agent identity) and endpoint, publishable/shareable via M365 Copilot, Teams, and the Entra Agent Registry (A2A protocol in preview). A distinct new agent runtime, identity class, and cross-tenant sharing/supply-chain surface Zenity must discover and govern separately from prompt-based agents

findings.title: Azure AI Foundry — Foundry Control Plane
findings.description: New unified control plane that tracks/manages agents from supported platforms across projects, with cross-project visibility, unified compliance enforcement, integrated security signals, and per-project TPM rate-limit / token-quota enforcement for model deployments. A new tenant-wide agent/model governance and inventory surface directly relevant to AISPM posture and policy-enforcement mapping

findings.title: OpenAI Codex Remote — GA phone→host agent control
findings.description: Codex Remote is now GA for all plans — an authenticated QR-paired channel that lets an iOS/Android device drive the Codex agent on a connected Mac/Windows host (start threads, send prompts, approve/deny commands, review diffs). A now-broadly-available off-device control plane for triggering and approving autonomous agent runs outside the monitored desktop — a new command-and-approval attack/abuse surface for red/purple teaming

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — DigitalOcean provisioning plugin
findings.description: New Codex plugin that connects a DigitalOcean account via OAuth and provisions/configures a Droplet (Codex Universal image, CLI/tooling/SSH pre-wired) as an on-demand remote workspace. A new agent cloud-provisioning connector — the agent can stand up and configure external cloud compute it then executes on, expanding the tool-execution and resource-access surface

findings.title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.142.2 — MCP tool-search default + native-path remote stdio MCP
findings.description: MCP tools now use tool search by default where supported (new default MCP tool-discovery behavior), and remote stdio MCP servers accept absolute working directories in platform-native path formats. New per-tool discovery and remote MCP working-directory surfaces on the local Codex endpoint that change which MCP tools an agent sees and where remote stdio servers operate

findings.title: Windsurf / Devin Desktop — Devin Local autonomous mode (v3.4.22)
findings.description: Devin Local (Rust-rewritten Cascade successor, on every tier incl. Free) gains an autonomous mode that runs the agent unsupervised and surfaces reviewable diffs before push, with subagents for subtasks. A new local unsupervised agent-execution surface acting on the codebase before human review — a new activity/data-flow detection surface for AIDR

findings.title: Windsurf / Devin Desktop — `/mcp` command + MCP status dashboard (v3.4.22)
findings.description: New in-session `/mcp` slash command with a live status dashboard over connected MCP servers. A new MCP tool-connection control/inspection surface on the endpoint that AISPM should account for when mapping which MCP servers/tools an agent can reach

platforms.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
details: **New agent experience (production-ready preview, June 2026)** — an enhanced orchestration runtime for improved response quality and reasoning, available alongside the classic experience. New agent build model/runtime. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/overview

**Microsoft IQ (June 2026)** — connects an agent to organizational data: emails, calendar events, files, Teams messages, and people information. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/use-microsoft-iq

**Skills (June 2026)** — modular, self-contained sets of instructions; created once, added to multiple agents, and exportable as a Markdown file or package to share. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/skills-overview

**Memory (June 2026)** — persistent per-user context that captures user preferences/patterns, stores them per user, and applies them over time. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/memory-overview

platforms.name: Claude Enterprise (Anthropic)
details: **Claude Tag (June 23, 2026)** — a new way for teams to work with Claude, starting in Slack where Claude joins as a team member. Teams grant @Claude channel access and connect it to chosen tools, data, and codebases; admins scope access per channel and can create separate Claude identities per use. Beta for Enterprise & Team. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/introducing-claude-tag

**Claude Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026)** — new agentic model (`claude-sonnet-5`) that plans, uses browsers/terminals, and runs autonomously near Opus 4.8 capability; available via Claude API, AWS, and Microsoft Foundry; default for Free/Pro. New tokenizer. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-sonnet-5

**Claude Science AI Workbench (June 30, 2026)** — a research environment that builds environments and manages compute on the user's laptop, cluster, or on-demand GPUs (asks before reaching new resources; reviewable/revocable), integrates researcher tools/packages, and renders scientific artifacts. Source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-science-ai-workbench

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI)
details: **Codex app 26.616 — Record & Replay + Thread handoff (June 18, 2026)** — Record & Replay (macOS) turns user-demonstrated workflows into reusable agent skills; Thread handoff moves conversations (with browser tab routing/annotations) between local and remote hosts. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/record-and-replay

**Codex CLI 0.141/0.142 (June 2026)** — per-thread stdio MCP servers (per-conversation MCP tool surface), Noise-relay E2E-encrypted remote execution, configurable multi-agent delegation modes (disabled / explicit-request-only / proactive), and indexed web-search mode. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog

**OpenAI Node SDK v6.45.0 (June 24, 2026)** — Realtime API "sideband call_id connections," Responses input-items + stream-accumulator helpers, and a tool-runner `afterCompletion` hook. Source: https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v6.45.0

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **iOS mobile app + Remote Control (June 29, 2026)** — native iPhone app (public beta) to launch/manage cloud and local agents with voice input, and to remotely direct a desktop agent (agent loop moves to cloud while tools keep running on the user's machine). Source: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/mobile

**Team/organization MCP marketplace distribution (June 30, 2026)** — admins configure Team MCP servers once and distribute them across cloud agents, IDE, and CLI via marketplace configs, gated by organization group access controls. Source: https://cursor.com/docs/mcp

**Automations: computer-use + new GitHub/Slack triggers (June 18, 2026)** — Automations can perform computer-use and be triggered by five new GitHub events plus a Slack emoji-reaction trigger; authorable in-session via `/automate`. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog
**Cloud subagents via `/in-cloud` (June 17, 2026)** — spawns isolated cloud subagents for parallel work with automated environment setup and reusable snapshots. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog

findings.title: Microsoft IQ (Copilot Studio)
findings.description: New organizational-data grounding connection that gives an agent access to emails, calendar events, files, Teams messages, and people information. Introduces a new knowledge-source / data-flow entity per agent — AISPM must discover IQ connections and map which agents can reach which org data (a prime overprivileged-agent / data-exposure toxic combination)

findings.title: Copilot Studio "new agent experience" (orchestration runtime)
findings.description: New production-ready agent build model with an enhanced orchestration runtime, running alongside the classic experience. A new agent type/runtime Zenity must inventory and govern distinctly from classic Copilot Studio agents

findings.title: Copilot Studio Skills
findings.description: New reusable, modular capability entity — a set of instructions created once, attached to multiple agents, and exportable/importable as a Markdown file or package. Introduces a shareable capability + supply-chain surface (a malicious or overbroad shared skill propagates across agents). AISPM must inventory skills and their agent bindings

findings.title: Copilot Studio Memory
findings.description: New per-user persistent memory store that captures and retains user preferences/patterns across interactions. A new data-at-rest entity holding user data/PII that must be inventoried, access-scoped, and monitored for sensitive-data retention

findings.title: Claude Tag — agentic Slack teammate with admin-scoped identities
findings.description: New Anthropic product (beta, Enterprise/Team) where Claude joins Slack as a member; teams grant @Claude per-channel access to arbitrary tools, data, and codebases, and admins can mint separate Claude identities per use. A new autonomous agent-identity + tool/data/codebase access surface inside a collaboration platform — Zenity must monitor agent identity governance, per-channel data exposure, and codebase reach

findings.title: Claude Sonnet 5 — autonomous agentic model
findings.description: New `claude-sonnet-5` model that plans, drives browsers/terminals, and runs autonomously near Opus 4.8 capability; distributed via Claude API, AWS, and Microsoft Foundry and set as the default for Free/Pro (new tokenizer). Cheaper autonomous tool-use drives broader agent deployment — a new model surface for red/purple-team coverage

findings.title: Claude Science AI Workbench — compute-provisioning research agent
findings.description: New app that builds environments and manages compute on the user's laptop, cluster, or on-demand GPUs (asks before reaching new resources; reviewable/revocable) and integrates researcher tools/packages. A new agent capability that provisions and executes on local/remote compute — an endpoint execution and resource-access surface

findings.title: Codex app 26.616 — Record & Replay + Thread handoff
findings.description: Record & Replay (macOS) converts user-demonstrated workflows into reusable agent skills; Thread handoff moves conversations (with browser tab routing/annotations) between local and remote hosts. New agent skill-authoring surface plus a local↔remote execution-boundary movement to monitor

findings.title: Codex CLI 0.141/0.142 — per-thread MCP servers, Noise-relay remote exec, delegation modes, indexed web search
findings.description: Plugin stdio MCP servers now activate per-conversation; remote execution runs over authenticated E2E-encrypted Noise relay channels; configurable multi-agent delegation modes govern sub-agent spawning; indexed web-search mode permits live search while restricting direct page access. New per-conversation tool-connection, remote-control transport, orchestration, and egress surfaces

findings.title: OpenAI Node SDK v6.45.0 — Realtime sideband + tool-runner hooks
findings.description: Adds Realtime API "sideband call_id connections," Responses input-items and stream-accumulator helpers, and a tool-runner `afterCompletion` hook. New agent tool-orchestration and Realtime-connection surface in the primary SDK proxy for the OpenAI API

findings.title: Cursor iOS app + Remote Control
findings.description: New native iPhone app (public beta) to launch/manage cloud and local agents (voice input) and to remotely direct a desktop agent — the agent loop moves to the cloud while tools keep executing on the user's machine. A new off-device control plane for triggering autonomous agent runs outside the monitored desktop/IDE

findings.title: Cursor team/organization MCP marketplace distribution
findings.description: Admins configure Team MCP servers once and push them across cloud agents, IDE, and CLI via marketplace configs, gated by organization group access controls. A new org-scale MCP supply/governance surface (which MCP tools reach whom) directly relevant to AI tool-connectivity posture

findings.title: Cursor Automations — computer-use + GitHub/Slack triggers
findings.description: Automations can now perform computer-use and be triggered by five new GitHub events plus a Slack emoji-reaction trigger, authorable in-session via `/automate`. Expanded autonomous tool-execution + event-trigger surface widens the agent-runtime attack/abuse surface

findings.title: Cursor cloud subagents (`/in-cloud`)
findings.description: New command spawns isolated cloud subagents for parallel work with automated cloud environment setup and reusable snapshots. A new cloud-side agent-execution surface (beyond the local IDE) to inventory and govern
